chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayoub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray by the side of the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and even though the prayer of the believers reaches him, from wherever they may be.'
ai.seo_question: Does prayer by the Prophet's grave reach him if performed elsewhere?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia practice of praying near the Prophet’s grave (Salat al-Qabr) as a means of seeking intercession and spiritual connection. It underscores the concept of *tawassul* (seeking means of approach to God) through the Prophet, affirming that the spiritual merit of the believer's prayer reaches him regardless of physical distance, thereby validating the veneration of the grave as a locus of divine proximity.
